answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer:
Yes, skip it. A long run takes two to three weeks to make you fitter, so a 16-miler on Wednesday can't help by Sunday. It would only leave you with tired legs and low fuel stores four days before the race.

You are already ready. In the last five weeks you ran two 20-milers, a 17 and a 15, and your numbers have not slipped:

| Run | Pace | Avg heart rate |
|---|---|---|
| Easy runs, last 4 weeks | 9:51–9:52/mi | 138–139 |
| 20 mi long run, Oct 4 | 9:59/mi | 146 |
| 12 mi long run, Oct 11 | 10:00/mi | 146 |

Same pace at the same heart rate means your fitness is holding. Wednesday's 4 marathon-pace miles also averaged 8:36/mi with no fade. The feeling of being ready will come from running 2 miles at 8:35/mi on Wednesday, not from more distance.

new.analysis:
**You ran last week exactly as planned.** All five runs matched the planned distances, for 34 miles total. The 4 marathon-pace miles on Wednesday averaged 8:36/mi with no fade, which is right on pace for 3:45.

**The heavy, dead legs are the most common complaint during a taper, not lost fitness.** With less running, your body repairs itself and refills its fuel stores, and that often feels sluggish before it feels sharp. Your "felt" scores slid from 7–8 to 5 as the miles came down, which is the usual pattern. Pain stayed at 0 the whole time.

**Race week cuts distance hard but keeps some faster running.** Fatigue clears faster than fitness fades, so about 16 miles before Sunday is plenty. One short run at marathon pace and a few strides keep your legs sharp. Monday and Friday stay as rest days so nothing feels new.

**Under 3:45 is within reach, but the last 6 miles are untested.** Your marathon-pace work has been at 8:33–8:40/mi for weeks, and threshold reps at 7:55–8:00/mi back that up. None of your long runs included marathon-pace miles, though, and your longest steady stretch at 8:35 was about 6 miles. That's why the pacing plan keeps the pace even and leaves any push until after mile 20.

| Section | Pace | Clock check |
|---|---|---|
| Miles 1–2 | 8:40–8:45/mi | about 17:25 at mile 2 |
| Miles 3–20 | 8:33–8:35/mi | about 1:52:30 at halfway, 2:51:40 at mile 20 |
| Miles 20–26.2 | hold 8:35, push only if strong | under 3:45 at the finish |

**If 8:35 already feels like effort 7/10 before halfway, ease to 8:45/mi.** That still finishes around 3:49, 13 minutes faster than your first marathon. Pace off the course mile markers, because watches usually read a little long over 26 miles.

**Try nothing new on race day.** Race in the Brooks Ghost 16 you wore for both 20-milers. Have the same breakfast and take the same fuel you used on those runs.
